description.narrative: The physical outputs of the Project will be (i) the rehabilitation or upgrading of the road network in South Tarawa, and (ii) trained and equipped community-based enterprises for road maintenance. The project will rehabilitate 32.5 kilometers (km) of main road and 10 km of feeder roads on the atoll of South Tarawa. The Executing Agency is Ministry of Finance and Economic Development and the Implementing Agency is Ministry of Public Works and Utilities.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. The government rehabilitates and upgrades the road network on South Tarawa. Indicator: By April 2013, 27.5 km of paved road and 6 km of unpaved road rehabilitated or upgraded to maintainable condition (average road roughness index no higher than 3 by 2013) Rehabilitated or upgraded roads are: (i) St. Anne to airport (21.5 km) and Temaiku spur (2.8 km) (ii) Betio and Bikenibeu roads (repairs) (iii) Betio Causeway (3.2 km) (iv) Feeder roads (6 km) Progress/Status: (i) Revised St. Anne(Bairiki) - airport (21.5km) and Temaiku spur (6.1km) - Achieved 35.5kms of paved road improved (increased over the original target due to increase in Betio) (ii) Betio and Bikenibeua roads (repairs) - achieved 11.4 km unpaved road paved. (iii) Betio loop and main road - achieved 1.8kms unpaved road improved (iv) Betio causeway -removed in 2015 from scope. Data Source: MFED's quarterly progress reports Target year: 2013

Output: 2. Community-based enterprises have the capacity to maintain the road network. Indicator: By May 2013, 6 community-based enterprises contracted to undertake road maintenance covering 45 km of road network Progress/Status: Maintenance approach changed to subcontracting 3 subcontractors engaged to cover whole road due to difficulties in establishing and recruiting enterprises in each community. Subcontractors are performing satisfactorily, including following road safety guidelines and practices. Data Source: MFED's quarterly progress reports Target year: 2013

Output: 3. The MPWU provides efficient implementation support. Indicator: Physical works completed by April 2013 within budget Progress/Status: Physical works completed on 28 November 2016 within revised budget following additional financing and project changes in 2015 and 2016. Data Source: MFED's quarterly progress reports Target year: 2013
The population has sustainable access to a safe, well-maintained road network in South Tarawa.

Adequate financing for road maintenance (base $1,000 per km, target $1,500 per kilometer by 2013) Progress/Status: --An annual budget of A$0.5 million is currently being provided up to November 2018 when the defects notification periods ends. A draft concept note for a Cabinet paper has been prepared addressing road maintenance options for 2019 and beyond, citing the need for A$0.415 million for annual maintenance. Data Source: Government accounts

Increase in average travel speed from 20 km per hour to 40 km per hour by April 2013 Progress/Status: Average speed increased to 31kph by end Nov 2017. 40kph speed limit extended in many villages addressing road safety. Physical civil works completed on 28 November 2016. Data Source: Project specific surveys by project consultants

Decrease in road casualties from 7 per year (2007) to 5 per year (2013) Progress/Status: Road casualties were between 1 and 5 between 2013 and 2016, although 12 were recorded in 2017; as these numbers are small, accidents with injuries are a better indicator - there was a significant increase in accidents from 20 to almost 200 in 2015 when project construction began, but this declined to 136 and 118 in 2016 and 2017, suggesting that the introduction of the road safety campaigns has had an impact. Data Source: Police and Ministry of Health statistics collated in the annual report of a road safety council
